title: R52 Step-0: grouped/batched execution probe on RTX 5090 (does grouping unlock low precision?)

torch_grouped_fp8.error: ValueError: torch._scaled_grouped_mm is only supported on CUDA devices with compute capability = [9.0, 10.0], or ROCm MI300+

conclusion: At nano d12 shapes (1 layer x 16 experts, dim=inter=384, T=2048) eager per-expert bf16 loops run at 36-45 TFLOPS; wrapping the same loop in a CUDA graph (launch-free) or batched bmm raises it to 83-105 TFLOPS (2.0-2.3x). Grouping fixes occupancy/launch, not per-tile efficiency: it is 2.3x, not 5x.
At full V4.1 expert shapes the eager loop is already 206 TFLOPS and grouping adds nothing (0.95-1.00x), so grouped execution only matters for the small nano shapes.

torch._scaled_grouped_mm (the official grouped FP8 path) refuses sm_120 outright: 'only supported on CUDA devices with compute capability = [9.0, 10.0]'. DeepGEMM's grouped/Mega MoE kernels are SM90/SM100-only as well, so a 5090 grouped FP8/FP4 kernel has to be written in TileLang/Triton; the official Mega MoE (FP8 activations x FP4 weights, SM100 tcgen05) is a design reference for layout/fusion, not a drop-in.
Combined estimate: grouped(+graph) bf16 on nano MoE GEMMs is the first 2x; FP8 on top needs the custom grouped kernel before its extra peak can show.
